short: Contrastive M/EEG decoding (M06) and subject-layer pooling (M03) were ahead in 2022 and are now standard; tests reuse training participants, and EEG headline and EEG zero-shot claims outrun the data.
position: The paper [@defossez2023] changes the decoding objective (M06, contrastive ranking of segments), the training population (M03, 175 participants in one model with a subject layer) and the target (M02, wav2vec 2.0 features). M06 and M03 were ahead: no earlier M/EEG decoder in the ledger ranks open candidate sets against a pretrained speech representation or uses a subject layer (Appendix); the subject layer helps on all four datasets, the contrastive loss on three (Tables 2–3). M02 is standard by cross-modal precedent from lip reading [@afouras2020asr; @ma2021lira]; on Brennan EEG it gains under one standard deviation over a learned Mel encoder. The evaluation (M12) is standard but never tests the subject layer on a new person. The MEG result holds within this protocol; the EEG headline figures, EEG zero-shot words and the parity with invasive decoders do not.
